digest.top_line: STAR-TREC: 12-mo TME-free survival 78.5% vs 60.6% (HR 1.90) with 50 Gy/25 fx LCCRT over 25 Gy/5 fx SCRT for organ preservation in mrT1-T3bN0 rectal ≤40 mm.
digest.tldr: Lower GI carried the day: in mrT1-T3bN0 rectal cancer ≤40 mm, 50 Gy/25 fx LCCRT raised cCR 64% vs 36% over 25 Gy/5 fx SCRT, favouring long-course CRT when organ preservation is the goal. Interim 12-mo read; 30-mo organ-preservation primary pending, and 22% of TME specimens were node-positive despite MRI N0.

sites.intro: Organ preservation in MRI node-negative early rectal cancer: randomised data on which RT schedule to pair with a watch-and-wait strategy.

studies.name: STAR-TREC

verdict.rationale: Governance-led interim at 12 mo; prespecified 30-mo organ-preservation endpoint not yet reached. Open-label, TME-free survival only, TME comparison non-randomised in phase 3.
verdict.audience: Rectal adenocarcinoma ≤40 mm, mrT1-T3bN0, no EMVI, ECOG 0-1

studies.significance: RT delivery does not explain the gap: completion was 99% with LCCRT and 100% with SCRT, with 18 (11%) needing a capecitabine dose change, so the difference tracks fractionation plus concurrent chemo, which this design cannot separate. Nodes in 22% of TME specimens despite MRI N0 make mesorectal coverage relevant; target volume is not in source text.
studies.monday_clinic: In MRI node-negative rectal adenocarcinoma ≤40 mm (mrT1-T3bN0) choosing organ preservation, this supports LCCRT over SCRT as the response-adapted backbone at 12 mo; it does not extend to EMVI-positive, node-positive, or >40 mm tumours.

primary_endpoint.name: TME-free survival at 12 months (interim)
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 1.90 (95% CI 1.29-2.81); 30-mo organ-preservation 1° EP not yet reported

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Open-label, randomised phase 2/3** at 37 sites in five European countries. Phase 2 randomised 1:1:1 to LCCRT-OP, SCRT-OP or primary TME (N=120); phase 3 used a **partially randomised patient-preference design**, with OP choosers randomised 1:1. Bayesian framework; this 12-month analysis covers 426 pts recruited before Aug 8, 2023 (409 mITT).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Rectal adenocarcinoma ≤40 mm, mrT1-T3bN0 on MRI**, ECOG 0-1, with primary TME judged reasonable. Excluded: MRI nodal involvement or EMVI, tumour within 1 mm of the mesorectal fascia, anterior tumours above the peritoneal reflection, predominantly mucinous histology, metastases. mrT2 in 242 (73%) OP pts; 266 (80%) below the peritoneal reflection.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **LCCRT-OP: 50 Gy in 25 fractions** with oral capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily. **SCRT-OP: 25 Gy in five fractions.** Response assessed at 16-20 weeks with TAE for near-complete response; target volume not in source text.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Phase 2 primary:** feasibility, recruitment at months 12 and 24 against thresholds of ≥4 and ≥6 randomisations/month (achieved 3 and 6). **Phase 3 primary:** organ preservation at 30 months (no TME, stoma or local recurrence), **not yet reported**. This analysis reports 12-month TME-free survival, response and safety.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Phase 2 alone gave **HR 3.7 (95% CI 1.7-8.0)**, with median TME-free survival 7.6 mo after SCRT-OP vs not reached after LCCRT-OP; pooling phase 3 pulled the estimate toward the null.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **Primary TME:** G≥3 SAEs in 14 (18%) of 78, intraperitoneal perforation from anastomotic leak in 12 (15%), and one postoperative death from sepsis. After TAE, perineal fistulation occurred in two (1%) OP pts. Capecitabine dose modification in 18 (11%) of 161.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: At design, **primary TME without neoadjuvant therapy was standard** for this population. OPRA addressed watch-and-wait after neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced disease; STAR-TREC is a randomised test of **which radiation schedule** best supports response-adapted organ preservation in smaller, node-negative tumours.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents MRI node-negative rectal adenocarcinoma ≤40 mm (mrT1-T3bN0), ECOG 0-1, fit for TME and choosing organ preservation. Does not represent EMVI-positive, node-positive, >40 mm, predominantly mucinous, or anterior above-reflection tumours.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The shrinking HR from phase 2 to the pooled cohort suggests early overestimation, and phase-difference analyses are **exploratory post-hoc**. Occult nodes in **17 (22%)** TME specimens imply MRI N0 misses nodal disease that organ-preserving arms never sample. Median follow-up was 34 and 35 mo, but outcomes were censored at 12 mo.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: At 12 months, a longer RT course with capecitabine buys **more complete responses and fewer TMEs** than SCRT, at the cost of more acute SAEs. What it does not settle is durable organ preservation, local regrowth and function, all tied to the 30-month endpoint.

studies.interpretation:
The question STAR-TREC answers at 12 months is narrower than organ preservation versus surgery, and more useful for it: in small, MRI node-negative rectal cancers where primary TME remains a reasonable default, which radiation backbone should a response-adapted pathway be built on. The answer favours long-course chemoradiotherapy with little ambiguity. TME-free survival was 78.5% with LCCRT-OP against 60.6% with SCRT-OP, the posterior probability of LCCRT superiority exceeded 99.5%, and the response data point the same way, with clinical complete response at the second assessment in 104 pts after LCCRT and 61 after SCRT. SCRT pts were more often sent to TAE for near-complete response, so the pathway was already compensating for the weaker response rather than manufacturing the gap.

How far to trust the magnitude is the harder question. The phase 2 estimate that prompted this report, HR 3.7, came from a small unmasked interim, and once phase 3 pts were pooled the estimate fell to 1.90 with a far narrower interval. The direction held and the magnitude contracted, which is how an early extreme estimate usually behaves, and the decision to publish at 12 months was taken after the committees had seen it. The Bayesian design removes the alpha-spending objection but not the concern about when to look. The endpoint also deserves scrutiny. TME-free survival is a clinician decision in an open-label trial, so any lower threshold for abandoning organ preservation after a short course would widen the gap without reflecting a difference in eventual tumour control. The authors themselves note that downstaging is time dependent.

The comparison with surgery is weaker evidence than the comparison between radiation schedules. Only phase 2 randomised pts to primary TME; in phase 3 the TME arm was self-selected, and 86% of phase 3 pts chose organ preservation. The surgical morbidity is still instructive: grade 3 or worse SAEs in 18% of TME recipients, intraperitoneal perforation from anastomotic leak in 15%, and one postoperative death. But it frames the stakes rather than measuring a randomised benefit. On the other side of the ledger, SCRT's advantage is acute, with grade 3 or worse SAEs within 4 weeks of radiation in 6% after LCCRT and 1% after SCRT. That is a real trade, but it is paid once, whereas a TME the schedule failed to avoid carries the morbidity the trial exists to escape.

Much of the organ-preservation experience, OPRA among it, comes from watch-and-wait after neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced disease; STAR-TREC moves the question to tumours for which the historical reference is surgery alone. That shift carries a staging risk the 12-month data cannot resolve. Nodal disease was found in 22% of TME specimens despite MRI excluding it, and organ-preserving pts never have those nodes sampled. Whether that becomes regional failure, and whether regrowth after complete response differs by schedule, belongs to the prespecified 30-month endpoint, which also counts stoma and local recurrence. The result would be wrong in the way that matters if organ preservation converges by then, or if function and late toxicity favour SCRT enough to offset the TMEs it fails to prevent early.
